newsitem.title: USA: New Jersey judge rules in favor of state & agency.
newsitem.headline: New Jersey judge rules in favor of state & agency.

text.p: A New Jersey judge on Wednesday ruled in favor of New Jersey and a state agency in an ongoing dispute over the construction of a $330 million highway in Atlantic City, a Superior Court official said.

The highway leads to land, called the H-Tract, on which Mirage Resorts Inc, Circus Circus Enterprises Inc and Boyd Gaming Corp plan to spend hundreds of millions of dollars to build huge, themed casinos.
The project's master plan, which includes the highway, is being developed by Mirage, and the state has agreed to help fund the highway's construction.

Several casino operators, however, including Trump Hotels & Casino Resorts, oppose state participation. They complain it is, in effect, a subsidy that gives Mirage and the others an unfair competitive edge in Atlantic City.

In a hearing last week, Trump's attorneys challenged the New Jersey Casino Reinvestment Development Authority's pledge to pay a $65 million share of the highway's cost. They argued the authority's plans violated New Jersey's constitution.
Judge Williams, however, disagreed in his order.
"Briefly, the judge ruled in favor of the state on all counts and declared none of the actions by the CRDA violated the constitution," a representative for Judge Williams told Reuters.
Details of the ruling were not immediately available.
In a statement from Las Vegas, Mirage Resorts expressed "its gratitude" for the Judge Williams' order.
Trump, also in a statement, said it would appeal the decision immediately and request the matter be sent to New Jersey Supreme Court on an expedited bases.
"A cursory revew of Judge Williams' opinion reaffirms our confidence that the (Supreme Court) will ultimately rule in our favor," Trump said.
